subject: Intermittent QPS dip on Dedicated GPU pool — investigation & customer pipeline plan
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@glyphtech.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ops@glyphtech.com
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observed QPS dip on our Dedicated pool at ~09:05 PST

Connor / Laura,

We saw two short dips in QPS for our production serving (dedicated pool GLY-prod-1) this morning around 09:05 and 09:18 PST. The failures manifested as 502/504 spikes for ~20s each and a broader 10% sustained drop for ~6 minutes. Our telemetry (attached) shows frontend retry storms around the same timestamps. Can you confirm whether this was a scheduling/autoscaler issue or something on the network side?

Attachments: metrics_snapshot_0905.png (image/png)

We'd like a short summary for our on-call and a timeline of what Redwood is doing — this is affecting a customer-facing pipeline and we need an ETA for mitigation and any credit/compensation process.

Thanks,
Sam Patel\Operations Lead, GlyphTech
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-18T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed QPS dip on our Dedicated pool at ~09:05 PST

Team — quick triage notes and immediate asks (will coordinate a customer-facing update after initial RCA):

1) Scope: reported dips on GLY-prod-1, two sharp 20s spikes (502/504), and a 6-minute ~10% throughput drop. Sam attached the metrics snapshot.
2) Immediate mitigation: if autoscaler isn't reacting, consider temporary manual scaling of GLY-prod-1 by +2 nodes and enabling the fast-path routing policy for that pool.
3) Logs: Ben, pull autoscaler controller logs from 08:50–09:30 and check for errors related to label matching and reconcile loops.
4) Networking: Laura, confirm there were no AZ-level network partitions for the reserved cluster in us-west-2.
5) Customer comms: I'll draft a concise status update to Sam once we have the root-cause indicator.

I'll open an incident (INC-20270418-GLY) and update the runbook link here. Please reply with initial findings ASAP.

—Connor\Director, Customer Reliability\Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-18T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed QPS dip on our Dedicated pool at ~09:05 PST

Connor — initial findings from autoscaler controller logs:

- At 09:04:57 the allocator reconcile loop failed with: "UnmarshalLabelSelector: unsupported key 'env:prod'"
- Controller retried reconcile but did not enqueue a scale event due to the selector parsing error, which prevented a scale-up for ~18s.
- After the parsing error was fixed by a hotpatch (09:05:20), the controller queued a scale, nodes joined by 09:05:38.

Pasted log snippet:
[2027-04-18T09:04:57Z] allocator: reconcile failure: invalid label selector 'env:prod' (parse error)
[2027-04-18T09:05:20Z] allocator: hotpatch applied -> selector normalization
[2027-04-18T09:05:38Z] allocator: scale event queued -> +2 nodes

Attachment: autoscaler-logs.txt (text/plain)

Initial RCA hypothesis: malformed label selector surfaced as parsing exception in the autoscaler controller binary after a recent config propagation (we shipped a label template change yesterday). That exception prevented the scale decision from executing for the short window and contributed to the 20s spike and the downstream retry storm.

Next steps: I will prepare a short, customer-friendly RCA and a remediation plan (fix to validation + config guardrail) and estimate time to full rollout.

- Ben\Senior SRE, Runtime
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@glyphtech.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Observed QPS dip on our Dedicated pool at ~09:05 PST

Sam — thanks for the quick flag and apologies for the disruption. Here is our high-level summary and immediate commitments: 

What happened (short):
- Root cause: an autoscaler controller parse error triggered by a malformed label selector template we recently propagated. That error prevented a timely scale-up for GLY-prod-1 and produced a brief 20s window of elevated 5xxs and a wider 6-minute throughput depression as clients retried.

What we did (immediate mitigation):
- Hotpatch to normalize selector handling deployed at 09:05:20 PST; scale event completed by 09:05:38 and normal throughput resumed.
- Enabled a temporary manual +2 node scale for your pool and enabled fast-path routing to reduce client retries.

Next actions and timeline:
- Short-term (24–48h): push a validation guard that rejects malformed selectors at propagation time; roll forward hotfix to all dedicated clusters (ETA: 24h).
- Medium-term (2 weeks): add selector schema checks to CI + pre-deploy linting to prevent similar config regressions.
- Ops support: we'll provide a runbook entry for your on-call team with detection rules and recommended client retry backoff adjustments.

Customer compensation and next steps:
- We will open an SLA credit request for the impacted window. Please use the attached SLA credit request form to capture billing details (attached).
- I'll schedule a 30-minute sync with your ops next week to walk through the timeline and answer follow-ups. Proposed slots: Tue/Wed 10–11am PST.

Attachments: sla_credit_request_form.pdf (application/pdf)
Runbook: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-glyphtech-qps-investigation

Let me know which slot works and any other immediate asks. Again, apologies — we're treating this with high priority.

Best,
Connor O'Brien\Director, Customer Reliability\Redwood Inference
From: Sam Patel <sam@glyphtech.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@glyphtech.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-20T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent QPS dip on Dedicated GPU pool — investigation & customer pipeline plan

Connor — thanks for the clear breakdown and the runbook link. The proposed timeslot on Wednesday 10am PST works for our team. Two quick follow-ups: 

1) Can you confirm the exact credit window you'll submit (start/end timestamps) so we can reconcile with our telemetry?
2) For the medium-term CI checks, will there be a short public summary of the guardrails or should we expect notes in the scheduled sync?

We appreciate the quick turnaround. Looking forward to the sync.

—Sam\Operations Lead, GlyphTech
